stem: Ishita models integers with tokens. She has $3$ positive tokens and must subtract $5$ positive tokens.

parts.text: Which move lets her complete the subtraction?

options.text: Rename her $3$ positive tokens as negative tokens, and remove nothing.
Add two zero pairs (each one positive and one negative token), then remove $5$ positive tokens; $2$ negative tokens remain.
Try to remove $5$ positive tokens at once even though only $3$ positive tokens are present, and add no zero pairs.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: She needs two more positive tokens to remove five, so she adds two zero pairs first, then removes five positives and is left with two negatives.

teacher.key_rationale: When positives to remove outnumber those present, add zero pairs first, then remove. Renaming positives as negatives, or removing without zero pairs, miss that step.
